title: parse_demo error returns discard the 3.3 spawn-class clones (and the partially-built Demo's other clones)
evidence: harness/demo.odin:264 `return {}, fmt.tprintf("bad spawn endpoints: %s", line)`; :272 `cls = strings.clone(fields[5])`; :259 `return {}, fmt.tprintf("bad spawn at-line (want: at <n>ms spawn <from> <to> [class]): %s", line)`; harness/main.odin:93-94 `for name in names { ok := run_demo(name, verb == "save", &cat, &rc); if !ok { failures += 1 }` — the loop continues to the next demo after a parse failure, so the process keeps running with the leaked allocations.
detail: Every parse_demo error path returns a zero-value Demo, discarding the partially-built struct. Any error after a successful spawn line (or spawn_node/place line) leaks the cloned class/type_name strings for the process lifetime — the 3.3 class clone (line 272) extends the pre-existing node/place clone pattern (lines 179, 307).
recommended_fix: On parse error, free the cloned strings of the partially-built Demo before returning (or parse into a temp and destroy on error).
